paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. Paul had a vision so amazing he was caught up to Paradise (2 Corinthians 12:2, 4), and then he was given a thorn in his flesh "to keep me from becoming conceited" (2 Corinthians 12:7). I think that stings a little, because being gifted and being humble don't always walk in together. Paul says the thorn was a messenger of Satan, sent to torment him, and he still doesn't hide it. He puts it right out in the open.

He pleaded with the Lord three times to take it away (2 Corinthians 12:8). Then the Lord says to him, "My grace is sufficient for you, for My power is perfected in weakness." (2 Corinthians 12:9). Friend, I would have wanted a different answer, maybe a full refund on the thorn! But the Lord gives Paul something better to hold onto, and that something is grace.

So what do you do with your own thorn, baker? You can quit hiding it and start leaning on Christ in it. Paul does, and he says he'll boast all the more gladly in his weaknesses, "so that the power of Christ may rest on me" (2 Corinthians 12:9). That's how he can say, "For when I am weak, then I am strong." (2 Corinthians 12:10). The weak spot you keep trying to cover up might be right where His power shows up the most.
